papers.title: The expected number of holes of the planar Wiener sausage
papers.summary: ```text Let $β_1^T(r)$ be the number of holes, that is, the first Betti number, of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ of a planar Brownian motion run up to time $T$. We prove that $\mathbb{E}[β_1^T(r)]$ is of order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$ as $T\to\infty$, for each fixed $r>0$, which completes the lower bound obtained in a companion paper from a law for the inradii of the cavities of the path. We also identify which parts of the complement of the path contribute at leading order. At unit time and radius $\varepsilon$, the holes lying in the unbounded component of the complement have expected number $O(\varepsilon^{-2+θ_0})$ for an absolute $θ_0>0$, whereas the additional holes created when a cavity fragments under erosion have expected number of exact order $\varepsilon^{-2}(\log(1/\varepsilon))^{-2}$. In particular the one-pocket constant of the lower bound is strictly improved. The upper bound is obtained by pricing the contact configurations that pin near-critical pockets along the two independent arms of the path from a deterministic time, each arm contributing one factor $1/\log(1/\varepsilon)$. The outer estimate combines a stratified form of this first-moment bound with a packing argument near the frontier of the path, and the splitting lower bound forces a dumbbell-shaped cavity by a local construction followed by two logarithmic avoidance probabilities. The upper bound and the two structural estimates use no limit theorem for the shapes of cavities; the shape law enters only through the lower bound of the companion paper. ```

papers.title: Phase transitions in the hard-wall large deviations for the Gaussian free field
papers.summary: We study the probability that the Gaussian free field on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\ge3$, stays above a level $-h_N$ throughout the lattice $N$-blow-up of a bounded Lipschitz domain, when $h_N$ is close to the entropic-repulsion height $\sqrt{4g_0\log N}$. Two mechanisms compete: a collective upward displacement of the field, whose cost is governed by capacity, and the suppression of the remaining local violations, whose cost is their expected number, both of which are of order $N^{d-2}/\log N$ exactly in the window $h_N(β)^2=g_0(4\log N+\log\log N+2β)$. We obtain a sharp asymptotic rate expressed through a variational problem combining a Dirichlet energy with an exponential potential inside this critical window. Outside this window we obtain the asymptotics at the appropriate moving speeds: capacity alone governs the cost as $β\to-\infty$, and the expected number of violations as $β\to+\infty$. As an application, we derive lower-deviation bounds for the cover level of a macroscopic body by random interlacements, which determine the order of decay at the transition.

papers.title: The strongly local part of nonlinear Dirichlet structures and its energy measures
papers.summary: This paper substantially extends the results of Sasaya (2026, JFA): we propose a framework for nonlinear generalizations of regular Dirichlet forms and prove that each energy in this framework has a largest strongly local part. We also prove the existence and uniqueness of canonical energy measures of this part, which satisfy convexity and locality properties and, under additional assumptions, certain chain rules in one variable. In particular, our framework requires neither $p$-homogeneity nor strong locality. Moreover, under a Ball--Carlen--Lieb-type upper bound, we prove more detailed chain rules for the directional derivatives of these energy measures. Our framework is applicable both to $p$-energy forms on fractals and to a class of symmetric nonlinear Dirichlet forms in the sense of Cipriani and Grillo~\cite{CG2003}, including those of Orlicz--Sobolev and variable-exponent Sobolev type.
papers.comment: 72pages, 2 figures. Comments are welcome. The author would be grateful for help identifying the ICMAT workshop participant mentioned in the acknowledgments

papers.title: Long-time behaviour of solutions for equations with randomness
papers.summary: We discuss results on the mixing properties of solutions for discrete and continuous time equations, drived by stationary bounded random forces, obtained during the last three years in a number or our joint papers. To facilitate applications of these results to specific equations with randomness, the results are edited and properly re-arranged.

papers.title: Poisson boundaries of lattices in locally compact groups
papers.summary: For a random walk on a general locally compact group we provide a discretization procedure transforming the walk to one on a lattice of the group, preserving the Poisson boundary and some finiteness of moments.

papers.title: Composite local observables of sine-Gordon via stochastic analysis
papers.summary: We develop a rigorous framework for the description of general local composite observables in Euclidean quantum field theories. The approach is nonperturbative and combines renormalisation group ideas with techniques of stochastic analysis. Via renormalisation dictated by sufficiently precise approximate solution theory of corresponding flow equations, we construct various local observables of the sine-Gordon model on the full space up to $β^2<6π$, including highly singular ones such as vertex fields $\exp(iαφ(y))$ in the optimal Wick regime $|\operatorname{Re}(α)|<4π/β$ and derivatives of arbitrarily high order, i.e. $\partial^μφ(y)$ for any multiindex $μ\in \mathbb{N}^2_0$. Applications of the approach include a direct proof of smoothness of observable-inserted correlation functions, and verification that the constructed objects satisfy a version of the prefactorization algebra axioms adapted to our setting.

papers.title: On the geometry of Gaussian Mean Shift Detection
papers.summary: We consider the problem of detecting a shift in the mean of a standard Gaussian random vector, where the direction of the shift belongs to an arbitrary subset $T$ of the Euclidean unit sphere. We introduce a correlation functional $κ(T)$ and establish a general lower bound on the detection radius in terms of this functional. We identify regularity conditions under which this lower bound is optimal up to an absolute constant. As an application, we recover some well-known results in the literature such as the detection radius for $s$-sparse unit vectors.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Operator Maps in Optimal Liquidation
papers.summary: We analyze the solution map of a optimal execution problem in which price dynamics are subject to a general transient impact kernel. Given the structure of the optimal trading strategy derived by Abi Jaber and Neuman in \cite{https://doi.org/10.1111/mafi.12465}, we show that the strategy is locally Lipschitz continuous with respect to the underlying model parameters governing temporary and transient price impact as well as the fundamental price process. Continuity of this map justifies the application of neural-net based approximations which take model parameters as inputs. We propose a method generating samples of the transient price impact kernel for the purposes of creating training data, and a method of projecting the kernel to a finite dimensional representation appropriate for input to a neural net, and a dimensional reduction based on the relationship between inventory and trade signal. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the trained neural net and use it to quantify the potential financial costs associated with misspecifying the transient impact kernel.

papers.title: Average and probabilistic linear widths of sequence spaces with a Gaussian measure
papers.summary: Let $γ$ be a Gaussian measure on the sequence space $\ell_2$ whose mean is zero and whose correlation operator $C_γ$ is a diagonal operator on $\ell_2$. Exact values of the $q$-average linear $n$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q<\infty$ are obtained. We also obtain asymptotic orders of the average linear $n$-width in $\ell_\infty$ under some condition on $C_γ$, and of the probabilistic linear $(n,δ)$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q\le 2$, and for $2<q\le \infty$ under some condition on $C_γ$.

papers.title: Integration by parts and DLR equations for SPDEs on the whole line
papers.summary: We study a stochastic reaction-diffusion equation on the whole real line, driven by space-time white noise, with a possibly nonlocal diffusion operator, such as a fractional Laplacian, and a coercive potential with polynomial growth. On the whole line, unlike on bounded intervals, its invariant measures cannot be described by an explicit density with respect to a Gaussian measure. We set the equation in suitable weighted spaces and show that invariant and infinitesimally invariant measures coincide, as do reversible measures and solutions to an integration-by-parts formula. We then show that the reversible measures are exactly the Gibbs measures defined through the Dobrushin-Lanford-Ruelle equations, without any moment condition, thanks to a priori estimates that also yield a Fernique-type theorem, uniform with respect to translations. In this way, we connect the Da Prato-Zabczyk approach to invariant measures of SPDEs with the DLR approach from statistical mechanics to Gibbs measures. Finally, we prove the existence of a reflection positive reversible measure and, in analogy with the one-dimensional long-range Ising model, we show that the reversible measure is unique, ergodic and translation invariant when the kernel of the nonlocal operator has a finite first moment, while it can be non-unique, for suitable double-well potentials, when the kernel has a power-law decay with infinite first moment.
papers.comment: 138 pages. Keys words: Gibbs measures; Dobrushin-Lanford-Ruelle equations; stochastic reaction--diffusion equations; invariant and reversible measures; integration by parts; nonlocal operators; long-range interactions; phase transitions

papers.title: A stochastic chemical system in contact with reservoirs
papers.summary: In this paper we analyse the behaviour of a non-reversible stochastic chemical system obtained as an approximation of a stochastic chemical system in which the concentration of some chemicals is higher than the concentration of the other chemicals. The master equation associated with this approximated system is characterised by a discrete part, modelling the reactions among chemicals that have low concentration, by a transport term and a diffusion term. The transport-diffusion terms describe the fluctuations in the concentration of abundant chemicals. The model contains a second order term is of order ε, that describes the fluctuation in the concentrations of the abundand substances. We prove that the master equation has a spectral gap that is independent on $ε$ and we analyse in detail the asymptotics of the solution to the master equation as $ε\to 0$.

papers.title: Random Laguerre tessellations in hyperbolic space
papers.summary: We introduce Laguerre tessellations in hyperbolic space as a weighted generalization of Voronoi tessellations and a hyperbolic analogue of Euclidean power diagrams. We present geometric and analytic constructions and establish conditions under which a collection of weighted points generates a well-defined tessellation. For Poisson point processes of weighted points, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions on the intensity measure ensuring that the resulting diagram is almost surely a tessellation. We then prove that hyperbolic Poisson-Laguerre tessellations are stable under intersections with totally geodesic subspaces, with an explicit transformation of the intensity measure. As applications, we identify the Poisson-Laguerre tessellations arising as sections of hyperbolic Poisson-Voronoi and ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellations. In particular, the latter have unbounded cells, while their proper totally geodesic sections have bounded cells almost surely.

papers.title: Energy Dissipation Along Trajectories and Wasserstein Gradient Flow of Aggregation-Diffusion Equations
papers.summary: In this work, we established the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations on bounded domains involving both nonlinear diffusion and nonlocal interaction effects. Our approach is based on stochastic analysis. More precisely, we investigated the associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) with normal reflection at the boundary from a trajectorial perspective and derived a semimartingale decomposition of the corresponding energy process. This decomposition leads to a trajectorial energy dissipation identity, which, together with the characterization of the metric derivative, allows us to establish the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of the aggregation-diffusion equation.

papers.title: On Monotonicity in Mean Field Games Induced by Discount Factor Transformations
papers.summary: This paper is devoted to the well-posedness of a class of infinite horizon discounted Mean Field Games (MFGs) problems, where both an exponential discount and a so-called cheap control factors are present simultaneously, and scale in a possibly different way. We introduce a new class of transformations of variables, at the level of both the MFG PDE and the corresponding FBSDE systems. We then show how these transformations reveal a new mechanism that generates semiconvexity estimates for the value function and ensures the existence of mean field equilibria, as long as the parameters land in a suitable regime, that we quantitatively describe. This new mechanism demonstrates furthermore how discount factors lead to a source of strong displacement monotonicity for the Lagrangian, without any initial monotonicity assumptions on the running costs. Consequently, in such regimes of parameters uniqueness of solutions manifests. Our approach uses a Lagrangian point of view, which lets us treat general non-separable Lagrangians and both deterministic and idiosyncratic noise driven models in a transparent, unified way. For a specific class of quadratic Lagrangians, using turnpike-type methods, we further obtain an exponential contractivity estimate for the mean field equilibria.

papers.title: Transforms between multivariate Laguerre and Meixner polynomials and their applications to gateways
papers.summary: We establish gateways in both directions between the Laguerre process and a discrete Markov process for every inverse temperature $2θ\geq 1$. Here, a gateway is an intertwining relation between Markov processes with continuous and discrete state spaces. A key ingredient is a pair of generating function identities that relate two double generating functions for multivariate Meixner polynomials to a single and a double generating function for multivariate Laguerre polynomials, respectively. These identities reveal a close relationship between the two families of polynomials and yield integral transforms that underlie the gateway relations. Gateway relations provide a means of transferring properties between continuous and discrete processes. As an application, we derive the Feller-Dynkin property and the uniqueness of the invariant distribution for the Laguerre process from the corresponding properties of the discrete process.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Formalism for Non-Invariant Probabilities: Entropy, Divergence, Channels
papers.summary: Let $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{M}_σ$ denote, respectively, the sets of Borel and $σ$-invariant probabilities on the uncountable set $Ω=\{1,2,...,d\}^\mathbb{N}$. Given a Hölder Jacobian $J$, the dual Ruelle operator $μ\in \mathcal{M} \mapsto \mathcal{L}_{J}^* (μ)$ will play the role of a dynamical channel; generalizes the action of a stochastic matrix on probability vectors. Since $\mathcal{L}_{J}^*$ generally breaks $σ$-invariance, we introduce the \emph{ni-entropy} $h_{ni}(μ)$ for non-invariant measures, employing the concept of the expected value function on cylinders of size one. $h_{ni}(μ)$ differs from Shannon entropy but extends the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy from $\mathcal{M}_σ$ to $\mathcal{M}$; $h_{ni}$ is concave and u.s.c. This leads us to the concept of ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}(A)$ of a potential $A:Ω\to \mathbb{R}$. $μ\in \mathcal{M}$ is not a density with respect to a dominating measure. We define an {\it ni-Kullback-Leibler divergence} $D_{ni}(ρ|| ν)$ not assuming absolute continuity. We investigate concepts of Information Theory such as Minimal Output Entropy, Donsker-Varadhan variational principle, a variational formula for $h_{ni}$, bounds for divergence, information projections, and their connections to the ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}$.

papers.title: Nonzero-Sum Stochastic Exit Games with Singular Belief Dynamics
papers.summary: We study a two-player nonzero-sum stochastic exit game with asymmetric information. Each firm chooses the time to exit a duopoly and, conditional on remaining active, when to exit a monopoly. The asymmetry stems from privately observed exit values, while profit flows are driven by a general one-dimensional diffusion. Allowing for exit from monopoly induces singular dynamics of the associated belief process, so we construct it as a limit of regular approximations. The underlying dynamics are not described by a system of SDEs, which requires a new mathematical approach. We construct a symmetric Nash equilibrium in which the duopoly exit is a hitting time of the belief process while the monopoly exit is described through the underlying diffusion. Our equilibrium exhibits novel phenomena: the market may be abandoned by both firms in finite time (market collapse), and firms with heterogeneous exit values may optimally exit simultaneously (clustering). These features are absent when monopoly is always preferred to exit.

papers.title: Uniqueness of generalized conformal restriction measures
papers.summary: We provide a new and unified approach (called the SLE arc test) for proving the uniqueness of generalized chordal and radial conformal restriction measures for $c\le 1$, where the $c<-2$ case is unknown before. This approach is inspired by the completely conformally invariant (CCI) measure introduced by Lawler and Werner (2000), and also by Cai's recent Green's function test for the Brownian loop catcher (2026).

papers.title: Besicovitch-like Pseudo Almost Automorphic Stochastic Processes: Theory and Applications to Semilinear SDEs
papers.summary: This paper introduces, for the first time, the concept of Besicovitch-like pseudo almost automorphic stochastic processes. As a meaningful application, we investigate a class of semilinear stochastic equations driven by Brownian motion in a separable Hilbert space. By combining the Banach fixed point theorem with refined inequality techniques, we establish sufficient conditions guaranteeing the existence, uniqueness, and global exponential stability of Besicovitch-like pseudo almost automorphic solutions in distribution for the considered equations. An example is provided to show the validity of the obtained results.

papers.title: Multivariate Bernstein duality for tournament Wright--Fisher diffusions
papers.summary: We give a probabilistic proof of a multivariate Bernstein duality for a multivariate Wright--Fisher frequency process with selection encoded by a finite tournament. The construction includes nontransitive interactions, such as rock--paper--scissors selection. Its dual is a pure-jump process of coefficient functions in the multinomial Bernstein basis. Selection increases the Bernstein degree through a winner--loser averaging operator, whereas neutral resampling decreases it through a duplication operator. For the proof, we construct a continuous forward process independently of duality, use duality to establish uniqueness, and obtain a weak stochastic differential equation representation and invariance of the simplex faces. This provides a sampling-based treatment of the tournament specialization of multitype Bernstein duality, extending an open problem in the binary Kingman setting of Cordero, Hummel, and Schertzer (2022).

papers.title: Stochastic homogenization of $p$-resistance forms on nested fractals
papers.summary: We study the stochastic homogenization of $p$-energies on infinite nested fractals. We assign i.i.d. random $p$-resistance forms $D_{0,α}$ to level-$0$ cells of an infinite pre-nested fractal, and study the scaling limit of the resulting random $p$-resistance form $\mathcal{D}^{(0)}$. Under a moment condition on the reciprocal of $D_{0,α}$, we prove that the sequence of rescaled and renormalized random energies is almost surely Mosco convergent to an equally weighted self-similar $p$-resistance form. As an application, when $p=2$, we prove the almost sure weak convergence of the associated rescaled continuous-time random walk. In particular, we allow arbitrarily small random conductances and impose no condition on the upper bound of random conductances.

papers.title: Mean Curvature Flow with Thermal Fluctuations in Dimensions Two and Higher
papers.summary:
Surface tension drives interfaces towards smaller area, while thermal motion produces shape fluctuations whose strength is linked to the interfacial mobility through the fluctuation--dissipation relation. These mechanisms lead to mean-curvature flow with thermal noise, whose graph formulation is known as the Kawasaki--Ohta equation. We establish global-in-time existence of energy martingale solutions to the spatially regularized Kawasaki--Ohta equation for periodic graphs in every dimension $d\geq2$, with initial data in $H^1(\mathbb T^d)$. No restriction on the noise intensity is needed for $d=2$, while a smallness condition is required for $d\geq3$. The key new challenges arise from the thermal noise, which has a $(1+|
abla u|^2)^{1/4}$-type coefficient. This coefficient gives rise to an irregular Stratonovich-to-Itô correction term of the form $
abla u\cdot D^2u
abla u/(1+|
abla u|^2)^{3/2}$. Our main innovation is a compactness argument tailored to the structure of the correction. By combining a factorization of this term with $H^1(\mathbb T^d)$ and area estimates, we establish strong convergence of the normalized gradients and reconstruct the weighted Hessian, which allows us to define the correction at energy regularity and identify its approximation limit.

papers.title: Rotating Walks, Derandomized Squares, and Permutation Conjugated Walks
papers.summary: Using the recent strong convergence results of Bordenave and Collins (Annals of Mathematics) and Chen et al. (Annals of Mathematics), we study the average case behavior of rotating random walks of Cohen and Maor (STOC 2023) and the derandomized square construction of Rozenman and Vadhan (RANDOM 2005). Concretely, we prove a conjecture of Cohen et al. (ITCS 2025) regarding the average case behavior of derandomized squaring for random graphs and show that the existential bounds of Cohen and Maor for their rotating random walk construction hold with high-probability for random graphs. Using the results of O'Donnell and Wu (FOCS 2020), we can in polynomial time construct a family of graphs and rotations which almost saturate the bounds of Cohen and Maor, and meet the bounds conjectured by Cohen et al. for all vertex-transitive auxiliary graphs of fixed degree in the derandomized square. Finally, we study independent random permutation conjugates of deterministic regular graph adjacency matrices. We prove quantitative weak convergence to freely independent tree adjacency operators when the degrees are fixed and the girths tend to infinity. Separately, a covering argument gives deterministic spectral lower bounds for polynomials with non-negative coefficients, recovering the lower bound of Cohen et al. for rotating walks.

papers.title: Tail Asymptotics for Gaps in Unitary Ensembles and the Airy Point Process
papers.summary: We derive tail asymptotics for the gap between the $k$th and $(k+1)$st largest particles, with $k$ fixed, in unitary ensembles and in the Airy point process. For the finite-$N$ ensembles, we consider the probabilities of a rescaled gap larger than $a_N$ and of a rescaled gap smaller than $b_N$, in the joint limits $N\to\infty$, $a_N\to\infty$ with $a_N=o(N^{2/3})$, and $N\to\infty$, $b_N\downarrow0$, respectively. For the Airy point process, the right and left tails are analyzed as the gap size tends to infinity and zero, respectively. More precisely, in both models, we obtain logarithmic right-tail asymptotics up to the constant term and cubic left-tail asymptotics with coefficient $k/6$. As an application, we also derive the limiting conditional laws of the leading particles given the existence of an abnormally large or small gap. In particular, for $k=1$, large-gap conditioning leads to a transition from Tracy--Widom to Gaussian fluctuations of the largest particle, similar to the BBP transition. Further, among any fixed number of leading gaps, we also determine the limiting probabilities of which gap attains a large maximum or a small minimum.

papers.title: Entropy maximization for cube projections
papers.summary: We prove that, in every dimension $n\ge150$, the one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz in these dimensions.
